item.title: Historic Inn Becomes Commons: Community restores 1901 landmark; raised to cut flooding risk

item.title: Supercooled clouds over the highest mountains respond differently to climate change
item.description: Most studies of how clouds are responding to climate change focus on clouds over the oceans, rather than over mountains. Those that do focus on mountain clouds tend to explore cloud microphysics rather than long-term trends in cloud phase. But understanding cloud behavior over regions such as the Tibetan Plateau, which supplies water to hundreds of millions of people, is critical—especially as diminishing snowpack and altered precipitation patterns threaten this critical water source. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wetland reclamation brings limited agricultural gains but high flood exposure
item.description: Wetland reclamation has long been regarded as a strategy to meet growing food demand, given the favorable soil and water conditions of wetlands. item.title: Ártico y Antártida pierden hielo: ¿qué significa para el nivel del mar?

Por su parte, un análisis internacional de IMBIE calcula que la pérdida de hielo de Groenlandia y la Antártida elevó el nivel medio global del mar en unos 3,1 centímetros entre 1979 y 2023. ¿Qué revelan estos datos sobre la evolución del deshielo y sus consecuencias para las zonas costeras? item.title: Japan issued a 9.9 magnitude earthquake alert, but ground didn't shake: What happened
item.description: An "alert" indicating a massive magnitude-9.9 earthquake sent shockwaves of fear across Japan on Friday afternoon. Just eight minutes after its issuance, the Japan Meteorological Agency retracted the warning, which had been triggered by a lesser magnitude-6.9 quake off the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia. Although the alert caused temporary disruptions in transportation, officials are now investigating the warning system to ensure public safety and prevent future confusion. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: About 2 billion metric tons of metal are produced worldwide every year to meet the demands of industry, infrastructure and the energy sector. item.title: Scorecard: Colombia gets top marks while high-emitting countries doing too little to protect health from climate change
item.description: The latest Healthy NDC Scorecard, published by the Global Climate and Health Alliance, finds that, Colombia integrates health most deeply into its national climate plan, closely followed by Nigeria and Cambodia. Conversely, the climate commitments of the governments of Japan, New Zealand and India fail to adequately consider health, while high-emitting economies, including EU members, China, Brazil and the U.K., refer to health in their national climate plans but do not match this with the ambitious emissions reduction targets required to protect health.
